title: Book: The Total Money Makeover — Dave Ramsey (2003)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Dave Ramsey's plan is a sequence of 'baby steps': build a small starter emergency fund, pay off all non-mortgage debt using the debt snowball (smallest balance first for motivation), grow a full emergency fund of three to six months of expenses, invest a fixed share of income for retirement, save for children's education, pay off the home, and then build wealth and give. He is strongly against credit cards and debt in general and stresses written budgets and behaviour change. Criticisms: the snowball can cost more interest than the avalanche method (highest interest first); his assumed long-term investment returns are considered optimistic; and refusing all credit can mean missing credit-score benefits. The step order and the emphasis on behaviour are the most useful parts; the numbers are US-specific.
